section3.intro: Techniques below are mapped to the tactic MITRE ATT&CK officially assigns them (current Enterprise matrix version), not an approximate grouping — several form the actual attack chain of a single scenario: credential theft in A/C opens the door to lateral movement in C, which enables collection and then exfiltration in D. Cross-references between sections reflect that continuity.

section4.title: 4. Incident Response Impact
section4.mttdBody: Per IBM's 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report (Ponemon Institute), the average global breach lifecycle — from initial compromise to full containment — is 241 days, the lowest figure in nine years, yet still far longer than this environment's Standard unified-audit-log retention window (180 days). In practice, a meaningful share of breaches detected at industry-average speed will already be losing their oldest logs before the investigation even begins.
section4.mttdBody2: With 0% Sentinel coverage, nothing correlates weak signals across products (a risky Entra ID sign-in, an anomalous endpoint action, an unusual Key Vault access) into one prioritized incident — pushing detection toward external notification rather than internal detection, the scenario IBM associates with the highest costs and longest timelines.
section4.mttrTitle: 4.2 Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) & Investigation Speed
section4.mttrIntro: Short retention windows compound the detection delay above into a resolution delay:
mttrBullets: Entra Sign-in Logs are capped at 30 days (portal, with P1) — past that window, without continuous export to Sentinel/Log Analytics, authentication history is permanently gone.
Defender for Endpoint advanced hunting (once licensed) is capped at 30 days native retention — Sentinel ingestion is required for anything longer.
Exchange Message Trace is capped at 90 days regardless of license.

Unified Audit Log Standard retention is 180 days — and audit logging is NOT on by default on SMB tiers (Business Basic/Standard/Premium); confirming it is actually enabled should be the very first IR action, before any retention discussion.
section4.mttrClosing: These short windows frequently force investigators to close cases as "inconclusive" once the retention window has passed, or to engage external DFIR firms to attempt reconstruction from backups, local Windows event logs, or third-party telemetry — an expensive option that's rarely complete.
